macro: Middle East tensions dominate overnight, with the UAE reporting two missiles launched from Iran, a vessel struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, and Tehran saying the Strait will stay shut until the U.S. meets interim-deal conditions while Trump says no talks with Iran are planned. The conflict is stoking oil worries and driving a broad selloff, with U.S. 30-year yields hitting their highest level since 2007 and a tech-led decline pulling Wall Street to two-week lows. The dollar is range-bound as markets price a potentially dovish Fed response, while July data showed a still-pressured housing market alongside rising factory output.
internals_narrative: Energy was the only clearly positive group (+1.0%) as DVN (+3.8%), PSX (+3.0%), CAT (+2.9%) and other energy/materials names led gainers, while Communication Services (-2.2%), Consumer Staples (-2.1%) and Technology (-1.7%) lagged and CHTR (-6.6%), STZ (-6.2%) and NOW (-5.1%) topped the losers. The rotation favored energy and materials over tech, staples and communication services.
